title: Gemini Flash-Lite for free users; effort can ‘use more of your limit’
key_facts: From the article date (9 Oct 2026), Gemini app users without a paid Google AI plan lose two of three models: free personal accounts move to Gemini Flash-Lite only, per Google's Gemini Apps Help page.
AI Plus subscribers (US $4.99 a month) keep Flash-Lite and Flash but lose Pro; AI Pro ($19.99) and AI Ultra subscribers keep all three. Google says AI Plus users will get an email on when it applies.
Google is adding low, medium and high effort levels for each model; its page says a higher level "will also use more of your limit".
Usage limits are compute-based and refresh every five hours up to a weekly cap; AI Pro subscribers will also get Deep Think.
9to5Google reported the change on 3 October; The Verge reported on 6 October that free users could still choose Flash-Lite, Flash and Pro.
Google released Nano Banana 2.1, an image model, on 6 October.
quote_evidence: Free personal accounts move to Gemini Flash-Lite only, according to Google’s Gemini Apps Help page.
This will increase the model’s ability to complete tasks and provide more thorough answers to queries, but will also use more of your limit.
The same day, The Verge reported that free Gemini users could still choose Flash-Lite, Flash and Pro.
why_it_matters_hint: Free Gemini users get only the smallest model and higher effort drains their limit faster.
event_date: Help page updated in the first days of October; first reported 3 Oct 2026 (9to5Google); said to apply from 9 Oct 2026
notes: Already carried in our 4 Oct 2026 edition (The Decoder, item 50). Newer details: start date "from today", effort levels, and the conflict with The Verge on 6 Oct.
